Balancing in Practice Start by adjusting total alkalinity to 80-120 ppm, which supports stable pH.
Total alkalinity (80-120 ppm) buffers pH against sudden changes.
Total alkalinity between 80 and 120 ppm stabilises pH and prevents rapid swings.
Without adequate alkalinity (target 80-120 ppm), pH swings wildly with every chemical addition or rainstorm.
In hot tubs, alkalinity tends to drift more than in pools due to aeration from jets, which off-gases CO2 and raises pH.
For any adjustment to alkalinity or pH, allow 4-6 hours before retesting.
Calcium hardness (200-400 ppm for plaster pools) protects pool surfaces and equipment.
Key Facts Target calcium hardness: 200-400 ppm for plaster and concrete pools; 150-250 ppm for vinyl and fibreglass.
Effects of Low and High Hardness Low calcium hardness (below 150 ppm in a plaster pool) causes etching and pitting of the pool surface, visible as rough patches.
Preventing and Removing Scale Prevention: keep LSI between -0.3 and +0.3 by maintaining pH below 7.6, calcium hardness at or below 400 ppm, and alkalinity at 80-120 ppm.
